chosen.cost: free, but it is then spent
chosen.name: Wind the pushrod in to minimum safe thread engagement

side_effects.pedal free play: goes to zero -- re-set the pedal stop so the cylinder still returns fully to its rest port, or the brakes will drag as they heat

chosen.cost: one fitting per cylinder, no performance penalty
chosen.name: Change the MC outlet from 'straight fitting + hardline bend' to '90 deg banjo'

side_effects.assembly: one more sealing joint per circuit to bleed and leak-check before the brake test
side_effects.pedal feel: unchanged -- this removes packaging length, not fluid

chosen.name: Move to a 'compact racing (short body)' cylinder body
requires_recheck: pedal_travel() stroke demand vs the new stroke limit

side_effects.lead time: a parts order sits on the critical path
side_effects.usable stroke: drops 6.4 mm to 19.0 mm -- only safe if pedal_travel() says the circuit needs less than that with a reserve

chosen.cost: pedal effort rises as the square of the bore ratio
chosen.name: Go up in bore, 15.9 -> 17.5 mm, and take the shorter-stroke cylinder it allows
requires_recheck: Hydraulic sizing: torque made vs needed at the new bore

side_effects.pedal force to reach lock-up: x1.21 -- check this against what a driver can actually push before you commit
side_effects.pedal travel to lock: x0.83 (shorter, the one genuinely free win here)

chosen.cost: geometry change; needs spherical rod ends
chosen.name: Tilt the cylinders to 10 deg off the X axis
requires_recheck: rod-end articulation through full pedal travel
hydraulic sizing at the higher pedal effort

side_effects.pushrod force reaching the piston: -1.5% (cosine loss), so pedal effort rises by about the same fraction
side_effects.side load into the bore: 17% of the rod load pushes sideways on the piston seal -- spherical rod ends at BOTH ends are mandatory past 3 deg

chosen.cost: pays for length and effort in travel
chosen.name: Raise the pedal ratio from 5.5 to 6.5 (clevis moves toward the pivot)
requires_recheck: brake pedal 2000 N check at the new clevis position

side_effects.clevis load: x1.18 into the bar and pushrod
side_effects.pedal effort to lock: x0.85 (lower -- this is the good half of the trade)
side_effects.pedal travel to lock: x1.18 (higher -- this is what it costs, and it is the half that gets forgotten)

f.message: The two circuits want different strokes (8.1 mm front vs 2.3 mm rear). They share one pedal, so the front circuit sets the pedal travel and the balance bar tilts to take up the difference. A large mismatch eats the bar's articulation and shifts bias as the pedal is pressed -- which is felt as a bias that changes with pedal effort.

The shortening plan leans on changes that cost pedal travel (Raise the pedal ratio from 5.5 to 6.5 (clevis moves toward the pivot)), and travel is already FAIL. Those two cannot both be paid for. Take the length out of the fittings and the cylinder body instead, or find it in the chassis.

Need 123.4 mm. SHORT BY 54.2 mm with 6 change(s):
    +8.0 mm  Wind the pushrod in to minimum safe thread engagement  (free, but it is then spent)
         -> pedal free play: goes to zero -- re-set the pedal stop so the cylinder still returns fully to its rest port, or the brakes will drag as they heat
         -> further adjustment: none left in this direction
    +28.0 mm  Change the MC outlet from 'straight fitting + hardline bend' to '90 deg banjo'  (one fitting per cylinder, no performance penalty)
         -> pedal feel: unchanged -- this removes packaging length, not fluid
         -> assembly: one more sealing joint per circuit to bleed and leak-check before the brake test
    +24.0 mm  Move to a 'compact racing (short body)' cylinder body  (buy different cylinders)
         -> usable stroke: drops 6.4 mm to 19.0 mm -- only safe if pedal_travel() says the circuit needs less than that with a reserve
         -> lead time: a parts order sits on the critical path
    +4.4 mm  Go up in bore, 15.9 -> 17.5 mm, and take the shorter-stroke cylinder it allows  (pedal effort rises as the square of the bore ratio)
         -> line pressure at a given pedal force: x0.83 (lower)
         -> pedal force to reach lock-up: x1.21 -- check this against what a driver can actually push before you commit
         -> pedal travel to lock: x0.83 (shorter, the one genuinely free win here)
    +2.5 mm  Tilt the cylinders to 10 deg off the X axis  (geometry change; needs spherical rod ends)
         -> pushrod force reaching the piston: -1.5% (cosine loss), so pedal effort rises by about the same fraction
         -> side load into the bore: 17% of the rod load pushes sideways on the piston seal -- spherical rod ends at BOTH ends are mandatory past 3 deg
         -> sanity: within the usual limit
    +2.3 mm  Raise the pedal ratio from 5.5 to 6.5 (clevis moves toward the pivot)  (pays for length and effort in travel)
         -> pedal effort to lock: x0.85 (lower -- this is the good half of the trade)
         -> pedal travel to lock: x1.18 (higher -- this is what it costs, and it is the half that gets forgotten)
         -> clevis load: x1.18 into the bar and pushrod
    -> Every listed lever is spent and it is still too long. This is a layout problem, not an adjustment problem: move the bulkhead, go to a floor-mounted pedal, or accept a different cylinder family.

findings.message: 99% front is outside everything these bores can make (60.7%-89.4%). No bar position gets there. Fit a smaller front bore or larger rear bore. Bias is set by the hardware; the bar only trims it.
The bar sits 0% off centre, so there is trim authority in both directions.

The two circuits want different strokes (7.3 mm front vs 1.9 mm rear). They share one pedal, so the front circuit sets the pedal travel and the balance bar tilts to take up the difference. A large mismatch eats the bar's articulation and shifts bias as the pedal is pressed -- which is felt as a bias that changes with pedal effort.

Master-cylinder body length came from the 'standard racing' catalogue placeholder (112.0 mm), not from your part. Put a caliper on the cylinder and pass mc_body_mm -- body lengths differ by 20.0 mm to 40.0 mm across families and that is most of the deficit you are chasing.

The line exit behind the cylinders is carrying 42.0 mm of the stack ('straight fitting + hardline bend'), which includes the bend radius the hardline needs to turn away from the cylinder. This is the segment most often missing from a CAD envelope check, because the fitting is modelled but the bend is not.
Fits with 105.5 mm to spare.
